title: POC weekly caching sync - CartFlow
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on prefix/KV cache hit rate improvements and prompt reuse strategy. Reviewed recent benchmark numbers (latency, token cost), discussed cache key strategy and TTL, and agreed on next steps: Redwood to share tuned caching config and perf spreadsheet; CartFlow to provide sampled traffic + golden prompts; schedule a controlled benchmark next week.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining the weekly caching sync for the CartFlow POC. We have about 45 minutes, agenda is quick updates, numbers, and next steps. Priya is here from Redwood to run through the KV and prefix cache tweaks.
[00:12] Daniel Park: Hey Alex, thanks. Quick note — Ran into a spike this morning on our checkout flows, so curious if the recent cache changes impact that.
[00:20] Priya Kapoor: Thanks Daniel, yeah we pulled the traces you sent last week and ran a warmup. Preliminary notes: overall prefix hit rate went from 12% to ~28% on the last run, KV-hit improved from 4% to 18% depending on TS windows, but there's variance by route.
[00:34] Maya Lopez: Wait 28% sounds great, but the checkout route is still low right?
[00:40] Priya Kapoor: Correct — checkout uses a lot of dynamic session tokens and cart-specific prompts so keys were very high cardinality. We suggested normalizing the prompt prefixes and moving ephemeral session fields out of the cache key which bumped that route from 3% to ~14%.
[00:55] Rohit Mehta: The spike I mentioned, we saw latency jump to 1.2s p95 on that route yesterday — baseline p95 was around 400ms. Could that be cache miss storming?
[01:05] Priya Kapoor: Possible, especially if many concurrent requests touch cold keys. Two mitigations we discussed: (1) small-time TTLs plus a background async warming for high QPS keys, (2) a per-route conservative pin for prefix cache for 1-2 minutes to avoid stampede. We can show config examples.
[01:20] Alex Chen: I'll pull up the perf sheet — link in the chat: https://redwood.internal/benchmarks/cartflow-caching-0902 (note: internal link). Numbers: overall token cost reduced ~12% week-over-week, latency p95 improved 9% overall, but as Priya said checkout still lags.
[01:38] Daniel Park: Can you remind us how the KV cache key is composed in the current POC image? I think our dev added user_id + prompt_hash + session_id which probably is too granular.
[01:48] Priya Kapoor: Yeah current key: userId|sessionId|promptHash|route. We recommend removing sessionId from the key and instead include a session-stable context hash where possible. Also canonicalize certain prompt fields (timestamps, UUIDs). That reduces cardinality.
[02:05] Maya Lopez: For the prompt reuse strategy, we're trying to reuse upstream system messages for 70% of calls. Is Redwood's prefix cache going to store system messages separately or together with user inputs?
[02:15] Priya Kapoor: Good question. Best practice is split: store system & assistant history in prefix entries where stable, then append user turn as delta. That means the prefix cache covers the expensive part of KV cache (long histories) and user tokens are short. In our tests that gave a big hit on threads where system prompts are reused.
[02:32] Rohit Mehta: Any concerns about correctness when removing sessionId? We need to ensure no leakage across users/sessions.
[02:37] Priya Kapoor: Absolutely, we only remove ephemeral session identifiers that are not security-critical. User identity (userId) stays in the key. We also recommend token-level encryption at rest and per-tenant isolation for Dedicated deployments.
[02:48] Alex Chen: Quick aside — security docs link is in the follow-up pack, folks asked for SOC2 controls earlier.
[02:55] Daniel Park: Great. Back to the numbers, do you have hit-rate breakdown by route?
[03:00] Priya Kapoor: Yes — sharing the high-level numbers: browse/search routes hit-rate ~42% prefix, 25% KV; recommendations route ~30%/12%; checkout route ~14%/6% after our last config. We'll attach the CSV.
[03:16] Maya Lopez: Is there a way to approximate cost savings by hit-rate? Even a ballpark per-million-reqs?
[03:21] Alex Chen: Rough ballpark: each cache hit avoids ~40-60 tokens on average for your workloads, so at 1M requests that can be ~40-60M tokens saved. At your committed pricing that maps to roughly $Xk — we'll put precise numbers in the sheet.
[03:36] Daniel Park: Okay good. On TTL strategy — what's the sweet spot you found? We need fresh product data but also want hits.
[03:42] Priya Kapoor: For product metadata we used 60s-300s depending on change frequency. For user personalization we used shorter TTLs (10-30s) and rely on cache warming for top keys. We also suggested ETag-style validation for heavier objects.
[03:55] Rohit Mehta: About cache warming: do you provide tooling or scripts to pre-warm?
[03:59] Priya Kapoor: Yes we can provide a small warmup job that hits top N keys. We'll include a python example in the repo. It uses your sample traces to compute top keys.
[04:10] Maya Lopez: For sampling traces — we'll drop last week's 24h trace in the shared folder. It's a bit big but should be fine.
[04:15] Daniel Park: We also want a controlled benchmark replicating the spike pattern. Can Redwood run that if we provide traffic traces?
[04:22] Alex Chen: Yes — we can run the benchmark in the Redwood Dedicated sandbox or on your staging. Prefer running it in our controlled harness so we can reproduce kernel-level metrics. We'll need signed access and a time window.
[04:33] Maya Lopez: Timeline? We want results within a week.
[04:35] Alex Chen: We can schedule a benchmark for Tues 09/09 if you provide traces by Thurs 09/04.
[04:42] Daniel Park: Works for us.
[04:45] Priya Kapoor: Quick tangent on eviction policy — by default we use LRU with weighted tokens; for your workload we recommended an adaptive policy that favors longer prefixes over tiny user deltas. That reduced churn in our runs.
[04:59] Rohit Mehta: Any changes needed in our client-side prompt construction? We currently include a lot of debug JSON in the prompt.
[05:05] Priya Kapoor: Yes, strip debug fields and move them to metadata. That reduces prompt size and helps canonicalization. Also replace absolute timestamps with relative ones where semantics allow.
[05:15] Alex Chen: Caught a question in the chat — "what about KV cache replication across regions?" Priya, quick answer?
[05:21] Priya Kapoor: We support cross-region replication options; for the POC we suggested collocating caches with primary read region to keep latency low, and asynchronous replication for metrics. If you need strict consistency, we can discuss per-route configs.
[05:33] Daniel Park: Any risks with async replication? Eventual consistency could show stale personalization.
[05:39] Priya Kapoor: Right — for personalization we keep sticky session reads to a region; replication is optimized for durability and analytics not commit-critical reads.
[05:47] Maya Lopez: On the model side — we tried a smaller quantized variant and saw token latency drop but slight quality diff. Did the caching interact with that?
[05:56] Priya Kapoor: Caching is orthogonal but helps obviate some quality regressions because repeated context is cached; however if generator variance increases (with smaller models) you might see different downstream behavior. We'll include per-model quality checks in the benchmark.
[06:12] Alex Chen: Alright let's get into action items — Priya, will you share the tuned config and the perf spreadsheet?
[06:18] Priya Kapoor: Yes, I'll share by EOD Friday 2025-09-05. Config will include example TTLs, key schemas, and warmup scripts.
[06:25] Daniel Park: We'll upload the sample traces and golden prompts by Thursday 2025-09-04.
[06:30] Rohit Mehta: I'll run a quick PR to remove debug blobs and push a client change by Wednesday.
[06:35] Maya Lopez: Could we also get a short doc on prompt canonicalization patterns?
[06:39] Priya Kapoor: Yep, short doc + examples included in the config bundle.
[06:43] Alex Chen: Great. Any other blockers or questions?
[06:46] Daniel Park: None from me. This was helpful.
[06:49] Alex Chen: Cool, recap of next steps in the chat. We'll sync up after the benchmark. Thanks everyone.
[06:55] (call ends)

Notes: Transcript contains typical ASR imperfections; some acronyms and proper names may be transcribed incorrectly (e.g., KV-cache sometimes appears as K-V cache, sessionId spelled session id, etc.). Attachments referenced: perf CSV, tuned caching config, warmup script (links shared in chat).
